A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Q3R work. Text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E are readable and matchable. The checklist present only in v1 is an identifiable removal, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: v1 reports original ViT training experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-1k, language-model fine-tuning on GLUE, and appendix ablations and computational measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Tables 1–12, Figures 1–3 and the experimental appendices.

M1.justification: The appendix computation procedures receive local corrections. Algorithm 4 changes its effective weighting from epsilon/max(sigma,1)-1 to epsilon/max(sigma,epsilon)-1 and reorganizes matrix products; Algorithm 3 replaces its square-root procedure with weighted sums. The defining Q3R objective and AdamQ3R training framework remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet-1k and GLUE coverage, including the Llama experiments in Appendix D.2. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Matched experiments retain the same unregularized, Adam, LoRITa, LoRA and dense fine-tuning comparators where previously evaluated. The appendix comparisons also retain their comparator membership; LoRa becoming LoRA is a spelling correction.

E3.justification: Sections 5 and D.1 retain the same training budgets, model configurations, augmentation, task metrics, batch sizes, hyperparameter searches and truncation settings. The appendix algorithm corrections do not establish that experiments were rerun or their evaluation settings changed.

E4.justification: Appendix E retains the same optimizer comparison and studies of regularization strength, target rank, reweighting period and low-rank initialization, with unchanged evidence in Tables 8–12.

E5.justification: Both versions retain D.1's selection of the best-performing configuration from three independent runs. Neither adds uncertainty estimates or significance tests. Removing v1's checklist assertion about statistical significance removes no actual statistical analysis.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 1–12 and curves in Figures 1–3 are unchanged. However, the abstract associates the same 1.3% and 4% accuracy drops with retaining 60% and 80% of parameters, whereas v1 describes removing those fractions. This changes the reported compression outcome in the summary, without establishing any experimental performance change.

T1.justification: Appendix A repairs a missing Z_ij squared factor in the positive-definiteness proof and explicitly defines zero padding of singular values. Appendix B corrects the regularizer-value derivation, including its factor of one-half and weighted terms. These are mathematical corrections; the majorization claim still lacks a proof in both versions.

C1.justification: The core contributions remain Q3R and AdamQ3R for low-rank pre-training and fine-tuning. The abstract changes its quantitative compression claim from removing 60%/80% of parameters to retaining those percentages, while Section 2 still claims a 60% reduction, introducing an internal mismatch.

C2.justification: The interpretations of hyperparameter sensitivity, initialization and computational overhead remain substantively unchanged. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning architectural scale, regularization choices and dense weight storage during training.

D1.justification: Appendices B–C provide revised computational instructions, explicit singular-value and smoothing inputs, elementwise-operation explanations and more detailed operation counts. Hardware, experimental hyperparameters, measured training times and the code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same underlying prior works and research positioning are retained. Consolidating duplicate LoRA references, updating Adam's bibliographic entry and shortening other references are bibliographic edits, not additions of research influences or changes in novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract and portions of the computational appendices, corrects language and terminology, standardizes bibliography formatting and removes the NeurIPS checklist. The main scientific narrative and section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: All three figures and twelve tables are retained, with some resized or relocated, including Table 1 and Figure 2. Algorithms 3–4 are reformatted, the total loss becomes a numbered display, and the supplementary material starts on a separate page.

improvement.justification: The appendix revisions improve correctness and reproducibility by replacing v1's invalid real square-root construction, restoring the regularizer's one-half factor and correcting the gradient threshold; Appendix A also repairs proof algebra. These localized technical gains outweigh the abstract's new confusion between parameters retained and removed. The empirical evidence remains unchanged.
